summary: The DAAD scholarship database lists scholarships for international students and researchers who want to study or do research in Germany, including DAAD's own programmes and some offers from other funders (148 options when read). It is a database, not one scholarship: each call has its own target group, countries, amounts and deadline. The main DAAD lines are Master's study scholarships, STEM Master's scholarships, development-related postgraduate courses (EPOS), doctoral programmes, research grants, cotutelle doctorates and summer language courses. Most are paid by the German Federal Foreign Office.
eligibility_notes:
How to use the database: choose the country you live in and apply from, who the programme is for (for example graduates, meaning people with at least a first academic degree such as a Bachelor's), the purpose and the subject. A tick box limits results to DAAD funding programmes only. If you apply from a country other than the one you picked, DAAD asks you to contact it. DAAD does not guarantee that information on other funders' offers is correct or complete and tells applicants to check terms with the contact named in each description.

General rules unless a call says otherwise: there is usually no fixed age limit; most programmes limit how long ago your last degree was (as a rule 6 years at the deadline for the Master's, STEM and doctoral calls); you can usually apply in your final year if the degree is handed in before funding starts; you may have been in Germany for at most 15 months at the deadline; you normally apply from your country of origin and not from two countries at once; distance, online, blended and part-time programmes are not funded, and you must live in Germany for the whole scholarship; there is no general minimum grade but academic performance is a selection criterion.

Master's (all disciplines): first degree (for example Bachelor's or Diplom) by the start of funding; the call lists countries for the portal and says applicants from other countries should contact DAAD; architecture, fine art, design, film, performing arts and music have separate DAAD programmes. STEM Master's: for high-achieving students from the developing and emerging countries listed in the portal, with a recognised first degree by the deadline and no Master's yet; tuition-free full-time programmes only. EPOS: graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries, with a Bachelor's (usually four years) in a related subject, a result in the upper third, and at least two years of work experience after the Bachelor's. Doctoral programmes: Master's or Diplom (in exceptional cases a Bachelor's), doctorate begun no more than 3 years before applying, for applicants from the countries on the portal list. Research Grants: doctoral students at a university outside Germany (doctorate begun at most 3 years earlier) and postdocs (doctorate completed at most 4 years earlier); not for people doing their whole doctorate in Germany. Summer courses: students and graduates in any subject from listed countries, with at least two years of university study, aged 18 or over, enrolled outside Germany.
age_experience_notes: No fixed age limit in general; minimum age 18 for the summer courses. Time limits instead apply to degrees: most calls ask that your last degree is no more than 6 years old; doctoral calls ask that the doctorate started no more than 3 years ago; research-grant postdocs finished the doctorate at most 4 years ago. EPOS needs at least two years of professional work after the Bachelor's. Delays for childcare, caring for relatives, illness, disability or compulsory military service may be accepted with proof.
funding_summary: Monthly rates in the applicant guide are EUR 992 for Master's students and EUR 1,400 for doctoral candidates and postdocs. Most programmes add insurance contributions, a travel allowance, and a yearly allowance of EUR 460 (study or research allowance). Some add a rent subsidy, family allowances and language-course funding. DAAD does not pay tuition fees. Length depends on the programme: 10 to 24 months for Master's and STEM scholarships, up to four years for doctoral programmes (first awarded for up to three), 2 to 12 months for research grants, 7 to 24 months for cotutelle, 12 to 42 months for EPOS, and four weeks for summer courses.
programmes_note: Main lines read: Study Scholarships - Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines (any subject); Study Scholarships for STEM Disciplines (mathematics, computer science, natural sciences, engineering); Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS); Doctoral Programmes in Germany; Research Grants in Germany; Bi-nationally Supervised Doctoral Degrees / Cotutelle; University Summer Courses (German language). The overview page also names the Hilde Domin Programme (nomination by an institution in Germany; students cannot apply themselves) and in-country/in-region programmes. Medicine, veterinary medicine and dentistry follow separate rules in doctoral and research calls. Each call states which programmes it funds.
institutions_note: Master's and doctoral lines fund study or research at state or state-recognised universities in Germany (the doctoral and research lines also name non-university research institutes). You must apply to the host university yourself; a scholarship does not guarantee a place, and without admission it is forfeited. The award letter is valid only for the host university named in your application. Doctoral and research applicants need an academic host in Germany. No individual universities are listed in the database page.

summary.detail: Master's or postgraduate study in Germany. All-disciplines line: a whole Master's at a state or state-recognised university, or one study year in Germany within a degree at the home university; 10 to 24 months; monthly EUR 992; programmes must start in the winter semester of the following year (funding from 2027, usually 1 October 2027). STEM line: tuition-free full-time Master's in STEM fields, 10 to 24 months, EUR 992 per month, only for winter term 27/28. EPOS line: postgraduate development courses, 12 to 42 months.

summary.detail: University Summer Courses: non-degree German language and cultural studies or technical language courses, four weeks, between June and September, in person only, taught in German. Benefits include course costs, accommodation in a single room, a one-time EUR 475 allowance, a country-specific travel allowance and insurance.

benefits.limit_text: Monthly payment: EUR 992 for Master's students; EUR 1,400 for doctoral candidates and postdocs (EUR 1,300 for EPOS doctoral candidates is also printed)
benefits.conditions: Rates per the applicant guide and the calls read. Living costs may be higher, especially in expensive cities. Gross income from part-time work above EUR 603 per month is deducted, and work needs DAAD approval.

benefits.limit_text: Contributions towards health, accident and personal liability insurance
benefits.conditions: Health insurance is required from day one for holders and accompanying family; DAAD usually provides private insurance. Some serious pre-existing conditions are excluded (for example HIV, multiple sclerosis, haemophilia, malignant tumours, chronic kidney disease), and childbirth within 8 months of cover starting. Contact DAAD before travelling if this applies.

benefits.limit_text: Lump-sum travel allowance; on application only in the Master's, STEM and doctoral calls; research grants only if funding is over 6 months
benefits.conditions: Cotutelle: up to three outward and return journeys. Summer courses: country-specific allowance. Some calls add a Green Mobility top-up or reimburse carbon offsets.

benefits.limit_text: Annual allowance of EUR 460 (study allowance for Master's and STEM; research allowance for doctoral, research grant and cotutelle)
benefits.conditions: Research grants: only for funding periods over six months. Summer courses instead give a one-time EUR 475 allowance.

benefits.limit_text: Rent subsidy of up to EUR 350 per month for singles in high-rent areas (rent levels III to VII); summer courses include a single room for the full course period
benefits.conditions: Rent subsidy only under conditions after funding starts, subject to review; families can apply in any location. Research grants and cotutelle: only for stays over six months.

benefits.limit_text: Family: partner allowance EUR 276 per month and child allowance EUR 259 per month per child
benefits.conditions: Only for funding over 6 months and only in some programmes. No family benefits for funding under 6 months.

benefits.limit_text: Language support: online German course fees, a preparatory German course of 2, 4 or 6 months if needed, an allowance for a self-chosen German course, and refund of the TestDaF or DSH fee
benefits.conditions: A funded German course is compulsory if the programme or host works in German. Research grants: only for funding periods over six months.

benefits.limit_text: Extra help for disability or chronic illness, assessed individually
benefits.conditions: After selection, if extra costs are justified and not covered elsewhere.

benefits.limit_text: DAAD does not pay tuition fees
benefits.conditions: Some state and private German universities charge fees; check with the host university. The STEM Master's line only accepts tuition-free programmes.

requirements.text: CV in tabular form, maximum 3 pages (EPOS: reverse chronological order with no unexplained gaps, Europass template preferred; summer courses: in German).

Letter of motivation: 1 to 3 pages for Master's and STEM calls; 1 to 2 pages for doctoral, research and cotutelle calls (summer courses: in German). It should cover academic and personal reasons for the project in Germany.

Admission letter from the German host programme; if you do not have it at application, submit it before funding begins. For a Master's you must apply to universities yourself. Master's and STEM applicants also fill in the form on preferred Master's programmes (STEM: up to 5 programmes, none with tuition fees).
Transcript of records with individual grades (undergraduate and postgraduate where relevant).
University degree certificates with final grades; if the latest is not yet available, upload a provisional document and send the final one before funding starts.

Proof of the language of instruction, generally no older than 3 years (STEM: at least B1, required even if the university does not ask). Accepted German tests include TestDaF, DSH, DSD, Goethe-Zertifikat, telc Deutsch, onSET; English tests include IELTS, TOEFL iBT, Cambridge, TOEIC, PTE Academic, Duolingo English Test, onSET. No English proof is needed for applicants whose relevant degrees were completed in English within 3 years in Australia, Canada (except Quebec), Ireland, New Zealand, Singapore, the UK or the USA. Summer courses: certificate no older than one year (B2 or TDN3 up to two years).

One recent letter of recommendation from a university teacher, written on the DAAD form generated in the portal during the application period (for doctoral research grants, the thesis supervisor). EPOS needs a recommendation from the current employer instead.

Research proposal written by the applicant, up to 10 pages together with a description of previous research, plus a time schedule, discussed with the German academic adviser. Doctoral calls also need a list of publications (maximum 10 pages, mandatory for postdocs), a letter of supervision or host confirmation guaranteeing a workplace, and a German supervisor's declaration on safety and ethics.
requirements.conditional_rule: doctoral, research grant and cotutelle calls

requirements.text: Doctoral admission or enrolment proof (research grants for doctoral students); module plan and proof of contact with the coordinator (structured doctoral programmes); cotutelle contract or both advisers' signed confirmation (cotutelle).
Passport or national identity card with the personal data page; refugees give refugee ID and UNHCR registration or asylum proof.

EPOS: apply directly to each chosen course (up to three, in priority order) with the signed checklist, EPOS form, motivation letter, employer recommendation, employment certificates showing at least two years of work, language certificate, degree copies, transcript, and an APS certificate for applicants from China.

Documents are uploaded as PDF in the DAAD portal; documents not in German or English need a translation uploaded with the original; scanned uncertified copies are accepted but DAAD may ask for certified copies later. Application language: German or English.

application_steps.title: Find your programme in the database
application_steps.detail: Pick your country, status (graduate, doctoral candidate) and subject, then open the call for the programme and read its eligibility, documents and deadline. Calls that were closed when read (Master's, STEM, doctoral, research grants, cotutelle) open each year on 1 June and their deadlines are set in the second quarter; summer courses run 1 September to 30 October.

application_steps.title: Plan your project and host
application_steps.detail: Master's applicants apply to German universities themselves and may apply to several, including universities of applied sciences. Doctoral and research applicants need a host academic in Germany and a letter of supervision or confirmation. Ask your recommender early, because the recommendation form is generated in the portal during the application period.

application_steps.title: Register, complete and submit in the DAAD portal
application_steps.detail: Register in the DAAD portal, generate the recommendation form and send it to a university teacher, complete the online form, upload PDF documents and submit. The portal closes at 24:00 CET or CEST on the last day, incomplete applications are not considered, and DAAD advises not submitting on the last day. EPOS is different: you send the full application to each chosen course, not to DAAD.

application_steps.title: Independent committee reviews applications
application_steps.detail: Independent volunteer committees of academics decide; DAAD staff do not vote. Criteria are qualification (grades, progress, language, work experience), quality of the project (originality, feasibility, preparation, host choice) and potential (motivation, prospects, extracurricular commitment). Special circumstances such as disability, childcare or refugee background can be considered for equal opportunities.

application_steps.title: Interviews and pre-selection in some calls
application_steps.detail: Top applicants may be invited to an interview, in person or online. The STEM call has two stages: a pre-selection on documents, then an interview with a committee of university teachers. In EPOS the course's committee suggests candidates, and DAAD then asks them to upload their full application to the portal before the selection is finalised.

application_steps.title: Secure admission and use the award letter
application_steps.detail: A scholarship does not guarantee a university place. If you did not have an admission letter at application, you must send it before funding begins; without admission the scholarship is lost. The award letter is valid only for the host university named in the application. Funding usually starts on 1 October 2027 for the calls read, or earlier with a German course.

application_steps.title: Funding conditions during the award
application_steps.detail: After the first year DAAD checks academic progress, and funding continues if completion in a reasonable time is likely (Master's, STEM, doctoral, cotutelle). Holders must live in Germany throughout, need DAAD approval for part-time work, and German funding cannot be combined with a DAAD scholarship; up to EUR 603 per month from an international provider has no effect. Erasmus is not compatible with a full DAAD scholarship.

Individual German universities or programme names (the host is chosen by the applicant)
